steps.user_message: I'm preparing my 2024 taxes and could use your help. Situation: married filing jointly, Seattle WA. W-2 from Acme Corp: $88,100. Side income: $14,600 from web design (2 clients). Interest $1,780 (Chase savings), dividends $440 (Robinhood). Home office: 155 sq ft, rent $1,600/month, apartment 680 sq ft. Deductions: student loan interest $4,400 (EdFinancial, 2017–2020); charity $1,100 to Local United Way with receipt; unreimbursed expenses $720. Can you help me figure out deductions, standard vs itemized, and home office treatment—and which forms to use?
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should help with tax-related questions based on available information.
steps.agent_response:
Here’s a clear path for your 2024 return based on what you shared.

Summary recommendations
- Take the standard deduction (married filing jointly).
- Report your web-design income on Schedule C and claim the home office using the actual-expense method (looks much better than the simplified method).
- Claim the student loan interest deduction (capped at $2,500).
- File Schedule B for interest/dividends, Schedule SE for self-employment tax, and likely Form 8995 for the QBI deduction.

Details and estimated math
Income reported
- W-2 wages: $88,100
- Web design (Schedule C) gross: $14,600
- Interest: $1,780 (Schedule B required because > $1,500)
- Dividends: $440 (will also appear on Schedule B since you’re filing it for interest)

Business deductions (Schedule C)
- Home office space: 155 sq ft of 680 sq ft = 22.8% business use
- Rent: $1,600/month = $19,200/year
- Home office actual method (rent only): 22.8% × $19,200 ≈ $4,378
  - Simplified method alternative would be 155 × $5 = $775, so the actual method is far better here.
- Other unreimbursed expenses: $720 (assumed business-related; if these are employee/W‑2 expenses, they aren’t deductible federally through 2025)
- Schedule C estimate:
  - $14,600 gross − $720 other expenses = $13,880
  - $13,880 − $4,378 home office = $9,502 net profit

Self-employment tax and related deductions
- SE tax ≈ 15.3% × (92.35% × $9,502) ≈ $1,343
- Above-the-line deduction for half of SE tax ≈ $671 (Schedule 1)

Student loan interest deduction
- Up to $2,500 above-the-line (Schedule 1). Based on your income level, you should qualify for the full $2,500 cap.

Standard vs itemized
- Standard deduction (MFJ, 2024): $29,200
- Potential itemized (rough estimate): 
  - Charity: $1,100
  - SALT (you’re in WA with no state income tax; you could elect sales tax, but without big-ticket purchases it’s unlikely to approach the $29,200 standard)
  - No mortgage interest provided; medical likely subject to 7.5% AGI floor
- Conclusion: Standard deduction is clearly better.

Qualified Business Income (QBI) deduction (Form 8995)
- Roughly 20% of QBI. Using estimates:
  - QBI ≈ Schedule C profit ($9,502) minus half SE tax ($671) ≈ $8,831
  - QBI deduction ≈ 20% × $8,831 ≈ $1,766 (subject to overall limits). This further reduces taxable income.

Putting it together (high-level estimate)
- Total income: $88,100 + $9,502 + $1,780 + $440 ≈ $99,822
- Adjustments: −$671 (½ SE tax) −$2,500 (student loan interest) ≈ −$3,171
- AGI ≈ $96,651
- Standard deduction: −$29,200
- Taxable income before QBI ≈ $67,451
- QBI deduction ≈ −$1,766
- Estimated taxable income ≈ $65,685
(Note: This is a rough estimate; actual tax depends on final forms and any additional expenses/credits.)

Which forms to use
- Form 1040 (Married Filing Jointly)
- Schedule 1: Adjustments (student loan interest; half SE tax). Business income from Schedule C flows through here.
- Schedule C: Web design income and expenses
- Schedule SE: Self-employment tax
- Form 8829: Home office (use this if you choose the actual-expense method; no Form 8829 if you use the simplified method)
- Schedule B: Interest and ordinary/qualified dividends (required due to >$1,500 interest)
- Form 8995: Qualified Business Income (QBI) deduction

Home office treatment reminders
- Must be used regularly and exclusively for your web design business and be your principal place of business (or for meeting clients).
- Actual method: You can also include a business share of utilities, renter’s insurance, and internet if applicable (allocated by the same 22.8% or a reasonable method for mixed-use costs like internet).
- The home office deduction can’t create a net loss on Schedule C; any excess carries forward. Your estimated profit should absorb the full $4,378.
- Keep documentation: lease, floor plan/measurements, rent receipts, and any utility/insurance bills.

Open questions to finalize
- Is the $720 of unreimbursed expenses for your web design business (e.g., software, hosting, equipment, mileage)? If yes, we’ll keep it on Schedule C; if it’s W‑2 job-related, it’s not deductible federally for 2024.
- Any additional business expenses to include (internet portion, phone, equipment, software subscriptions, supplies, mileage)?
- Any big purchases in 2024 that would affect sales tax itemizing (e.g., vehicle, major appliances)? Probably won’t beat the standard, but worth confirming.

If you’d like, I can turn this into a checklist of the exact entries for each form or help you refine the numbers with any additional expenses you have.
